files.content:
---
name: fibe-tool-agent-defaults-get
description: Use when you need to read the installation or Team default Agent configuration before creating or changing an Agent.
---
# fibe_agent_defaults_get

Returns the effective default Agent settings: provider, model, enabled skills, mounted files and prompt defaults.

## Inputs

- `scope` (optional): personal or Team owner of the defaults.

## Notes

- Read before `fibe_agent_defaults_update` so an update starts from current values.

---
name: fibe-tool-agent-defaults-reset
description: Use only when the user asks to discard customised Agent defaults and return to the shipped defaults.
---
# fibe_agent_defaults_reset

Resets Agent defaults for the selected owner to the installation baseline.

## Inputs

- `scope` (optional): personal or Team owner of the defaults.
- `confirm`: must be true.

## Notes

- This is destructive for customised defaults; confirm with the user first.

---
name: fibe-tool-agent-defaults-update
description: Use when the user wants to change default provider, model, skills or mounted files for new Agents.
---
# fibe_agent_defaults_update

Patches the default Agent configuration. Only supplied fields change.

## Inputs

- `patch`: object of default fields to change.
- `expected_revision` (optional): reject the change if defaults moved meanwhile.

## Notes

- Existing Agents keep their own settings; defaults apply to Agents created afterwards.

---
name: fibe-tool-agents-activity
description: Use when you need the recent activity timeline of an Agent, such as tool calls, status changes and artefacts.
---
# fibe_agents_activity

Lists recent activity entries for one Agent conversation.

## Inputs

- `agent_id_or_name`: Agent ID or name.
- `limit` (optional): number of entries.

## Notes

- Prefer `fibe_agents_live_state` for the current status; activity is a history.

---
name: fibe-tool-agents-create-conversation
description: Use when you need a new conversation with an existing Agent without sending a message yet.
---
# fibe_agents_create_conversation

Creates or upserts an Agent conversation and returns its identifier.

## Inputs

- `agent_id_or_name`: Agent ID or name.
- `title` (optional): conversation title.

## Notes

- Use `fibe_agents_start_chat` when you also want to send the first message.

---
name: fibe-tool-agents-delete-conversation
description: Use only when the user explicitly asks to delete an Agent conversation.
---
# fibe_agents_delete_conversation

Deletes one conversation and its stored messages.

## Inputs

- `agent_id_or_name`: Agent ID or name.
- `conversation_id`: conversation to delete.
- `confirm`: must be true.

## Notes

- Deletion cannot be undone.

---
name: fibe-tool-agents-duplicate
description: Use when the user wants a copy of an Agent with the same configuration under a new name.
---
# fibe_agents_duplicate

Duplicates an Agent's configuration, skills and mounted files. Conversations are not copied.

## Inputs

- `agent_id_or_name`: source Agent.
- `name` (optional): name of the copy.

## Notes

- Credentials bound to the source Agent are not copied.

---
name: fibe-tool-agents-interrupt
description: Use when an Agent run must stop, for example when it is looping or the user changed their mind.
---
# fibe_agents_interrupt

Interrupts the active run of an Agent conversation.

## Inputs

- `agent_id_or_name`: Agent ID or name.
- `conversation_id` (optional): conversation to interrupt.

## Notes

- The conversation stays available; send a new message to continue.

---
name: fibe-tool-agents-live-state
description: Use when you need the current status of an Agent: idle, running, waiting for input or failed.
---
# fibe_agents_live_state

Returns the live state of an Agent and its current run.

## Inputs

- `agent_id_or_name`: Agent ID or name.

## Notes

- Poll sparingly; prefer `fibe_monitor_follow` for streams.

---
name: fibe-tool-agents-messages
description: Use when you need to read the messages of an Agent conversation.
---
# fibe_agents_messages

Lists messages of one conversation, newest last.

## Inputs

- `agent_id_or_name`: Agent ID or name.
- `conversation_id` (optional): defaults to the latest.
- `limit` (optional).

## Notes

- Message content may be long; request a small limit first.

---
name: fibe-tool-agents-runtime-status
description: Use when you need to know whether an Agent's runtime is provisioned and healthy on its Host.
---
# fibe_agents_runtime_status

Returns runtime provisioning and health information for an Agent.

## Inputs

- `agent_id_or_name`: Agent ID or name.

## Notes

- A failed runtime usually needs `fibe_doctor` or a Host check, not a new message.

---
name: fibe-tool-agents-send-message
description: Use when you need to send a message to an existing Agent conversation.
---
# fibe_agents_send_message

Sends one user message to an Agent conversation and returns the accepted message.

## Inputs

- `agent_id_or_name`: Agent ID or name.
- `message`: text to send.
- `conversation_id` (optional).
- `attachment_paths` (optional): files to attach.

## Notes

- The reply arrives asynchronously; read it with `fibe_agents_messages`.

---
name: fibe-tool-agents-start-chat
description: Use when you want to start a new conversation with an Agent and send its first message in one step.
---
# fibe_agents_start_chat

Creates a conversation and sends the initial message.

## Inputs

- `agent_id_or_name`: Agent ID or name.
- `initial_message`: first message.

## Notes

- Returns the conversation identifier for later reads.

---
name: fibe-tool-artefact-upload
description: Use when you need to publish a file produced during work, such as a report, screenshot or build output, as an artefact.
---
# fibe_artefact_upload

Uploads a file as an artefact owned by the current Agent or user.

## Inputs

- `file_path` or content: the file to upload.
- `name` (optional): display name.
- `agent_id_or_name` (optional).

## Notes

- Never upload secrets or credential files.

---
name: fibe-tool-auth-set
description: Use when the local MCP session needs a different API key or server profile to talk to Fibe.
---
# fibe_auth_set

Stores an API key for the local profile used by this session. The key is never echoed back.

## Inputs

- `api_key`: key to store.
- `profile` (optional): profile name.
- `server` (optional): server URL.

## Notes

- Ask the user for the key; never invent or print keys.

---
name: fibe-tool-call
description: Use when no dedicated tool exists and you need to call one Fibe operation directly by name.
---
# fibe_call

Calls one named Fibe operation with JSON arguments and returns its result.

## Inputs

- `operation`: operation name from `fibe_tools_catalog`.
- `arguments`: JSON object.

## Notes

- Check the operation shape with `fibe_schema` first.

---
name: fibe-tool-doctor
description: Use when Fibe tools fail unexpectedly and you need to diagnose authentication, connectivity or configuration.
---
# fibe_doctor

Runs local diagnostics: server reachability, authentication, profile and version checks.

## Inputs

- None.

## Notes

- Share the summary with the user; it never includes key values.

---
name: fibe-tool-feedbacks-get
description: Use when you need the details of one feedback item left on a Playground or Agent result.
---
# fibe_feedbacks_get

Returns one feedback entry with its comments and status.

## Inputs

- `feedback_id`: feedback identifier.

## Notes

- Use `fibe_feedbacks_list` to find identifiers.

---
name: fibe-tool-feedbacks-list
description: Use when you need to review feedback left by people on Playgrounds or Agent output.
---
# fibe_feedbacks_list

Lists feedback entries, optionally filtered by Playground, Agent or status.

## Inputs

- `playground_id_or_name` (optional).
- `agent_id_or_name` (optional).
- `status` (optional).

## Notes

- Address open feedback before reporting work as finished.

---
name: fibe-tool-find-github-repos
description: Use when you need to find a GitHub repository connected to Fibe before importing or launching it.
---
# fibe_find_github_repos

Searches connected GitHub repositories by name or owner.

## Inputs

- `query`: text to match.
- `limit` (optional).

## Notes

- Only repositories visible to the connected installation are returned.

---
name: fibe-tool-get-github-token
description: Use only when a git operation inside a Playground needs a short-lived GitHub token for a connected repository.
---
# fibe_get_github_token

Returns a short-lived, repository-scoped token for git operations.

## Inputs

- `repository`: owner/repo.

## Notes

- Never print, log or commit the token; use it only for the immediate git command.

---
name: fibe-tool-gitea-repos-create
description: Use when the user wants a new private Gitea repository managed by Fibe.
---
# fibe_gitea_repos_create

Creates a Gitea repository on the Fibe-managed git server.

## Inputs

- `name`: repository name.
- `private` (optional): defaults to true.

## Notes

- Prefer `fibe_greenfield_create` when you also want a Playground.

---
name: fibe-tool-github-repos-create
description: Use when the user wants a new GitHub repository created through the connected installation.
---
# fibe_github_repos_create

Creates a GitHub repository through the connected installation.

## Inputs

- `name`: repository name.
- `owner` (optional).
- `private` (optional).

## Notes

- The installation must have permission to create repositories.

---
name: fibe-tool-greenfield-create
description: Use when the user wants to start a brand-new project: repository, Spec and Playground in one step.
---
# fibe_greenfield_create

Creates a new repository from a starter, a Spec for it and optionally launches a Playground.

## Inputs

- `name`: project name.
- `provider` (optional): github or gitea.
- `template_id_or_name` (optional): starter Spec.

## Notes

- Gitea greenfield repositories are private by default.

---
name: fibe-tool-help
description: Use when you are unsure which Fibe tool fits a task or how a tool is meant to be used.
---
# fibe_help

Returns extended help on Fibe concepts and tools.

## Inputs

- `topic` (optional): tool or concept name.

## Notes

- `fibe_tools_catalog` lists every tool; this tool explains them.

---
name: fibe-tool-launch
description: Use when the user wants to launch a new Playground from a Spec, a repository or a Compose document.
---
# fibe_launch

Launches a new Playground from a Spec, a repository URL or Compose YAML.

## Inputs

- `template_id_or_name` or `repository_url` or `template_body`.
- `name` (optional).
- `host_id_or_name` (optional).
- `variables` (optional).

## Notes

- For an existing Playground use `fibe_playgrounds_switch_template` instead of launching again.

---
name: fibe-tool-local-playgrounds-info
description: Use when you need to know which Playground the current local directory is linked to.
---
# fibe_local_playgrounds_info

Returns the Playground link stored for the local project directory.

## Inputs

- `directory` (optional): defaults to the current directory.

## Notes

- Use `fibe_local_playgrounds_link` to create a link.

---
name: fibe-tool-local-playgrounds-link
description: Use when you want to link the current local project directory to a Playground.
---
# fibe_local_playgrounds_link

Stores a link between a local directory and a Playground so later tools can default to it.

## Inputs

- `playground_id_or_name`: Playground to link.
- `directory` (optional).

## Notes

- The link is local configuration only.

---
name: fibe-tool-logs-follow
description: Use when you need to stream logs of a Playground service while reproducing a problem.
---
# fibe_logs_follow

Streams service logs until the timeout or line limit is reached.

## Inputs

- `playground_id_or_name`: Playground.
- `service` (optional): service name.
- `timeout` (optional).

## Notes

- Prefer `fibe_playgrounds_logs` for a one-off tail.

---
name: fibe-tool-memorize
description: Use when you learn a durable fact about the user's project that future Agent runs should know.
---
# fibe_memorize

Stores a memory entry with tags and optional groundings.

## Inputs

- `content`: the fact.
- `tags` (optional).
- `idempotency_key` (optional).

## Notes

- Never store secrets as memories.

---
name: fibe-tool-monitor-follow
description: Use when you need to follow live events, such as Agent messages, activity or artefacts, for a while.
---
# fibe_monitor_follow

Streams monitor events for selected types until a timeout.

## Inputs

- `types` (optional): message, activity, mutter, artefact.
- `timeout` (optional).

## Notes

- Use `fibe_monitor_list` for a snapshot.

---
name: fibe-tool-monitor-list
description: Use when you need a snapshot of recent monitor events across Agents and Playgrounds.
---
# fibe_monitor_list

Lists recent monitor events.

## Inputs

- `types` (optional).
- `limit` (optional).

## Notes

- Filter by type to keep results short.

---
name: fibe-tool-mutter
description: Use when you want to post a short progress note that people watching the Agent can see.
---
# fibe_mutter

Posts a short status note, a mutter, for the current Agent.

## Inputs

- `message`: short note.

## Notes

- Keep mutters brief and free of secrets.

---
name: fibe-tool-mutters-get
description: Use when you need to read recent progress notes posted by an Agent.
---
# fibe_mutters_get

Returns recent mutters for one Agent.

## Inputs

- `agent_id_or_name`: Agent ID or name.
- `limit` (optional).

---
name: fibe-tool-pipeline-result
description: Use when you need the cached result of an earlier pipeline run.
---
# fibe_pipeline_result

Returns a cached pipeline result by identifier.

## Inputs

- `pipeline_id`: identifier returned by `fibe_pipeline`.

---
name: fibe-tool-pipeline
description: Use when a task needs several Fibe operations in sequence and you want them run as one pipeline.
---
# fibe_pipeline

Runs a declarative pipeline of steps, with variables and iteration.

## Inputs

- `steps`: list of operations.
- `variables` (optional).

## Notes

- Read the pipeline schema with `fibe_schema` first; results are cached for `fibe_pipeline_result`.

---
name: fibe-tool-playgrounds-action
description: Use when a Playground needs a lifecycle action: start, stop, restart, rebuild or destroy.
---
# fibe_playgrounds_action

Performs one lifecycle action on a Playground.

## Inputs

- `playground_id_or_name`: Playground.
- `action`: start, stop, restart, rebuild or destroy.
- `service` (optional).

## Notes

- Destroy needs explicit user confirmation.

---
name: fibe-tool-playgrounds-debug
description: Use when a Playground is failing and you need its combined diagnostic picture.
---
# fibe_playgrounds_debug

Returns status, recent events, failing services and log tails for a Playground.

## Inputs

- `playground_id_or_name`: Playground.

## Notes

- Start debugging here before reading individual logs.

---
name: fibe-tool-playgrounds-logs
description: Use when you need the recent log lines of a Playground service.
---
# fibe_playgrounds_logs

Returns a bounded tail of service logs.

## Inputs

- `playground_id_or_name`: Playground.
- `service` (optional).
- `lines` (optional).

---
name: fibe-tool-playgrounds-switch-template
description: Use when an existing deployed Playground must move to a different Spec or Spec version, for example after changing its services.
---
# fibe_playgrounds_switch_template

Switches an existing deployed Playground to another Spec or Spec version and redeploys it in place. This is the normal tool for changing the stack or service/source shape of a running environment.

## When to use

- Adding, removing or renaming services.
- Changing labels, images, build settings or volumes of an existing Playground.
- Moving a Playground to a newer version of its Spec.

## Inputs

- `playground_id_or_name`: Playground ID or name of the deployed Playground.
- One of `template_id_or_name`, `template_version_id`, `template_body` or `repository_url`: the target Spec.
- `variables` (optional): values for template variables.
- `changelog` (optional): note stored on a newly created Spec version.

When the target uses repositories that do not exist yet, the switch provisions private Gitea repos for them, so the Playground keeps working source.

## Notes

- Volumes are kept unless the new Spec removes them.
- Use `fibe_playgrounds_wait` afterwards, then `fibe_playgrounds_debug` if services fail.
- To start a new environment instead, use `fibe_launch`.

---
name: fibe-tool-playgrounds-wait
description: Use when you must wait until a Playground reaches a state such as running before continuing.
---
# fibe_playgrounds_wait

Waits until the Playground reaches the requested state or the timeout passes.

## Inputs

- `playground_id_or_name`: Playground.
- `status` (optional): defaults to running.
- `timeout` (optional).

## Notes

- On timeout, continue with `fibe_playgrounds_debug`.

---
name: fibe-tool-repo-status-check
description: Use when you need to check whether a repository is connected, reachable and ready for launches.
---
# fibe_repo_status_check

Checks repository connection, default branch and access.

## Inputs

- `repository`: owner/repo or URL.

---
name: fibe-tool-resource-delete
description: Use only when the user explicitly asks to delete a Fibe resource.
---
# fibe_resource_delete

Deletes one resource by type and identifier.

## Inputs

- `resource`: resource type.
- `id_or_name`: resource identifier.
- `confirm`: must be true.

## Notes

- Deletion may be irreversible; confirm first.

---
name: fibe-tool-resource-get
description: Use when you need the full record of one Fibe resource by type and identifier.
---
# fibe_resource_get

Returns one resource.

## Inputs

- `resource`: resource type.
- `id_or_name`: resource identifier.

## Notes

- Secret values are always redacted.

---
name: fibe-tool-resource-list
description: Use when you need to list Fibe resources of one type, such as Playgrounds, Specs or Hosts.
---
# fibe_resource_list

Lists resources of one type with optional filters and paging.

## Inputs

- `resource`: resource type.
- `query` (optional).
- `page` (optional).

---
name: fibe-tool-resource-mutate
description: Use when you need to create or update a Fibe resource that has no dedicated tool.
---
# fibe_resource_mutate

Creates or updates one resource with a JSON payload.

## Inputs

- `resource`: resource type.
- `operation`: create or update.
- `id_or_name` (update only).
- `payload`: JSON object.

## Notes

- Check the operation shape with `fibe_schema` before mutating.

---
name: fibe-tool-run
description: Use when you need to run a command inside a Playground service container.
---
# fibe_run

Runs one command in a Playground service and returns its output.

## Inputs

- `playground_id_or_name`: Playground.
- `service`: service name.
- `command`: command to run.

## Notes

- Output is bounded; redirect large output to a file.

---
name: fibe-tool-schema
description: Use before calling an operation when you need its exact JSON input shape.
---
# fibe_schema

Returns the JSON Schema for one Fibe operation or resource.

## Inputs

- `resource` or `operation`: what to describe.

---
name: fibe-tool-status
description: Use when you need a quick overview of the account: authentication, Hosts, Playgrounds and Agents.
---
# fibe_status

Returns a short account and session status summary.

## Inputs

- None.

---
name: fibe-tool-templates-change
description: Use only when you must edit Spec versions directly without touching any deployed Playground.
---
# fibe_templates_change

Hidden advanced primitive. Edits a Spec by creating a new version from patch edits or a full body. It does not redeploy anything.

Normal existing deployed Playground stack/source/service changes do not belong here: use `fibe_playgrounds_switch_template` with the Playground, which creates the version and redeploys in one step.

## Inputs

- `template_id_or_name`: Spec to change.
- `edits` or `template_body`: patch edits to apply, or the complete new body.
- `changelog` (optional): human-readable note for the new version.

## Notes

- Validate the body against the `fibe-template-schema-json` skill first.
- Existing Playgrounds keep running their current version until switched.

---
name: fibe-tool-templates-search
description: Use when you need to find an existing Spec to launch or adapt.
---
# fibe_templates_search

Searches Specs by name, category and description.

## Inputs

- `query` (optional).
- `category` (optional).

---
name: fibe-tool-tools-catalog
description: Use when you need the list of available Fibe tools and their modes.
---
# fibe_tools_catalog

Returns the catalog of tools available in this session.

## Inputs

- None.

---
name: fibe-tool-update-name
description: Use when the user wants to rename the current Agent or conversation.
---
# fibe_update_name

Updates the display name of the current Agent or conversation.

## Inputs

- `name`: new name.
